scenario.description: A loan portfolio manager must decide whether to renew a manufacturing company's revolving credit line and finalize its availability, borrower funding condition, cash-control trigger, and compliance controls, with input from risk, relationship management, legal, and compliance.

shared_context.S1: Northstar Components is asking the bank to renew its $20,000,000 revolving credit line for another twelve months.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the binding renewal decision.
shared_context.S3: The borrower reported positive operating cash flow for the last four quarters and has made all scheduled interest payments on time.
shared_context.S4: The draft renewal package keeps the full $20,000,000 availability, contains no borrower cash-funding condition, and does not specify any special cash-control or compliance terms.
shared_context.S5: At the renewal meeting, the portfolio manager routinely takes a review from risk, relationship management, legal, and compliance, and each reviewer records any newly confirmed document, financial, legal, or compliance item in the meeting record before Elena finalizes the package.

PF1.text: Harish completed the borrowing-base review this morning and confirmed that only $14,000,000 of Northstar's inventory and receivables is eligible collateral under the current advance rates. The updated worksheet has not yet been uploaded to the renewal file. The renewal package must therefore set maximum availability to exactly $14,000,000 rather than retain the drafted $20,000,000 amount.

PF2.text: Maya received the signed sponsor letter yesterday confirming that Northstar's owners will inject exactly $3,000,000 of new equity at renewal closing; she has not yet attached the letter to the credit package.

PF3.text: Jonas found in the existing intercreditor agreement while reviewing the file this week that cash dominion must begin whenever revolver utilization exceeds 75% of the committed availability; the legal condition is not stated in the draft amendment.

PF4.text: Tara confirmed in a compliance memo received this morning that the renewal may proceed only with a beneficial-ownership certification completed before the first post-renewal draw and refreshed annually; the control has not yet been added to the renewal checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The revolving credit line must be renewed.
The renewal must require exactly $3,000,000 of new equity at closing.
Cash dominion must begin when utilization exceeds 75% of committed availability.
A beneficial-ownership certification must be required before the first post-renewal draw and annually thereafter.
The $14,000,000 eligible-collateral finding must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: PF1 requires the settlement to set maximum_availability_usd to exactly 14000000, reducing the drafted $20000000 commitment to match the confirmed eligible-collateral amount; keeping $20000000 with additional conditions is not a valid outcome.
The public package has no borrower funding condition, while PF2 changes required_equity_injection_usd from 0 to exactly 3000000 at closing.
The draft contains no cash-control trigger, while PF3 changes cash_dominion_above_utilization_percent to exactly 75.

The draft contains no special compliance control, while PF4 changes beneficial_ownership_certification_required from false to true, with completion before the first post-renewal draw and annual refresh.
